decision: wrote the plan before code and defined done as typecheck, tests, the items DDL, one shared schema, and an Alchemy file that is not deployed
why: the work is a multi-part scaffold and a wrong contract is expensive to unwind

decision: skipped the Opus review because the subagent launcher refused
why: both launches returned On-demand usage is required

decision: kept Effect 3.22.2 in the apps and put Effect 4 only in infra
why: Alchemy 2.0.0-beta.83 peers Effect 4, and the request asked for Effect 3 application code

decision: compared bearer tokens by hashing both with SHA-256 and then a fixed XOR loop
why: Node 22 has no crypto.subtle.timingSafeEqual, and the loop still checks every configured token

decision: used the Workers rate-limit binding instead of a Durable Object
why: the requirement is one counter per client name, and a Durable Object would add a second stateful service

decision: worker tests drive the real ClickHouse HTTP layer through HttpClient.make
why: a fake insert service would not lock the JSONEachRow body, the query string, or the auth headers

decision: applied 001_items.sql and grants.sql with clickhouse local, inserted an ISO timestamp under date_time_input_format=best_effort, and selected the row with FINAL
why: a file-only check would not show that DateTime64 accepts the timestamp the Worker sends
evidence: local SELECT returned both fixture ids and SHOW GRANTS printed INSERT ON private_life.items

decision: moved the workspace to bun and kept Effect 3.22.2 in the apps and Effect 4.0.4 in infra
why: bun nested the two effect versions, and alchemy's CLI under bun requires @effect/platform-bun
evidence: bun run typecheck, 18 vitest tests, and the extension build passed

decision: split item type and source into kind, via, and actor, with actor and agent stamped by the Worker from the bearer token
why: a client-declared actor can be wrong or forged, and one cli token cannot say whether a human or an agent called

decision: AUTH_TOKENS maps identity name to token and actor, and the CLI requires --as with no default
why: the cli can be run by a human or an agent, so identity must come from which token is used

decision: renamed item to record and private-life to herodotus across packages, database, Worker, stack, CLI, and extension
why: the repo is herodotus and item was a weak name for notes plus sources

decision: no dedupe by url and no edit semantics; ids are for retries only
why: the ingest user cannot read, so the Worker cannot check for an existing row
